description.narrative: ADSA has valuable experience in implementing sustainable development projects, particularly in the agriculture and forestry sectors. We have collaborated with international organizations such as Germany/EU/GIZ on the CEEGA II project (2024-2025) to promote organic agricultural production and integrated livestock systems. Our projects have the ultimate goal of reducing production costs, increasing output, ensuring food diversity, and increasing villagers' income. Furthermore, we have strengthened nutrition work by involving multiple sectors. In this project ADSA aim to advocate for government agencies (policymakers) to contribute and promote the advancement of Climate-smart Clean Agriculture (CSCA) production, in order to progressively address issues forpoor people and improve their livelihoods step by step. Specific Objective 1: To strengthen provincial, district, and village-level local authorities and community leaders so that they are capable and dedicated to motivating and encouraging private sector producer groups to participate in the implementation of state policies and socio-economic development plans, ensuring gradual and tangible results. Specific Objective 2: To increase the production output of people in the project's two target villages,making their production more efficient and effective, and to significantly reduce methane (CH4) emissions, estimated at an average of approximately 9-11% of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from agricultural production released into the environment.

Experience in Sustainable Agriculture and Forestry The ADSA Association has valuable experience in implementing sustainable development projects, particularly in the agriculture and forestry sectors. We have collaborated with international organizations such as Germany/EU/GIZ on the CEEGA II project (2024-2025) to promote organic agricultural production and integrated livestock systems. Our projects have the ultimate goal of reducing production costs, increasing output, ensuring food diversity, and increasing villagers' income. Furthermore, we have strengthened nutrition work by involving multiple sectors. 2. Experience in Environmental Policy and Natural Resource Conservation In 2023-2024, ADSA received a grant from the French Embassy in Laos to implement a project for the conservation and protection of a wetland area (Oubeung). This project aimed to strengthen gender relations whilepromoting sustainable ecosystem management. We organized peer support groups, strengthened village development committees, established local trainer teams, and promoted organic home garden vegetable cultivation. Through various activities, we were able to improvethe livelihoods of poor families and establish capable teams to lead villagers in implementing agroecological principles. 3. Experience in Community Development and Emergency Response to Crises We have solid experience implementing the COVID-19 response project (CiSAC-19) during 2019-2022. This project was directed and coordinated bythe Lao Civil Society Coordination Committee (LCCO) and supported with funding from the European Union (EU). We utilized development tools such as Advocacy and SBCC (Social and Behavior ChangeCommunication) to change community behaviors, protect public health, and promote a new, sustainable, and safe way of living. 4. Experience in Collaboration with Domestic and International Partners ADSA has a strong history of collaboration with leading funding agencies such as Swisscontact, ALISEA, UNDP, FAO, WFP,the World Health Organization, CARE, Save the Children, and GOAL International. Furthermore, we have close linkages with the government sector, including the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Labour and SocialWelfare, local authorities, local enterprises, and other civil society organizations. This extensive collaborative experience enables us to implement various projects effectively and achieve objectives comprehensively.
